content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: SLO breach detected for service=redwood-runtime, endpoint=/v1/streaming/generate, window=5m, p95=2.3s, p99=12.1s (>10s threshold). Investigate. Dash: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/latency-streaming

Eve (oncall): paging ack. jumping in. any ETA on scope?

Mike (infra): I'm seeing a tight correlation with heavy IO on gpu-pool-2 hosts. NVMe queue depth spikes + cgroup writeback. possible noisy neighbor. pulling metrics now.

Sara (ML): confirmed from traces: a lot of sends stuck in stream_kv_fetch; tail gets a full stall (~8-12s) when p99 spikes. attach example trace ids: trace=abc123, trace=def456. streaming chunk delays show huge gaps.

Josh (support): Customer acme-inc reported multiple streaming timeouts at 14:02 UTC. They saw stalled chunks and the websocket timed out after 30s. They want status.

Eve (oncall): assign remediation priorities: 1) stop customer impact, 2) restore SLO, 3) root cause. Propose immediate mitigation: isolate high-IO tenants on gpu-pool-2, and enable fallback routing to dedicated small-gpu-1 for critical traffic.

Mike (infra): quick fact-check: current pool usage: 84% gpu util, 68% memory, NVMe utilization at 95%. Top contributor tenant: tenant_id=tenant-998 (approx 400 concurrent streams). Recommend cgroup throttle for tenant-998 and move their pods to burst queue.

Sara (ML): is tenant-998 running a large .mpt model? that'd explain KV cache thrash I/O.

Mike (infra): yes, looks like they pinned a fp16 model with large context. KV cache miss rate is huge.

Eve (oncall): Mike, can you apply a temporary cgroup limit and add tenant-998 to soft-isolate? steps?

Mike (infra): doing now. commands:
```bash
# add tenant to cgroup with reduced io weight
sudo cgcreate -g blkio:/noisy-tenant-998
echo "500" | sudo tee /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/noisy-tenant-998/blkio.weight
# move process (example PID 4210)
sudo cgclassify -g blkio:noisy-tenant-998 4210
```
Applying in 2m.

Eve (oncall): also flip routing fallback for critical routes to dedicated-slate-1. deploy-bot, can you run the safe-routing rollback?

deploy-bot: routing change started (task id: rchg-20260314-11). Routes: /v1/streaming/generate for tier=enterprise -> dedicated-slate-1. Canary 10% -> 50% over 3 mins.

Anna (PM): flagging impacted customers: acme-inc (enterprise), betahouse (standard). Notify acme-inc support thread with ETA estimate after mitigation.

Josh (support): notifying acme-inc now: "we've detected elevated tail latency and are applying mitigations; short-term routing to dedicated pool; will update in 10m".

Mike (infra): cgroup applied. watching IO metrics. NVMe queue depth dropped ~60% after moving main PIDs. gpu-pool-2 IO util down to 55%.

Sara (ML): tracing after cgroup move: gaps reduced. example trace abc123 now shows streaming chunk gaps ~200ms not >8s. Looks like KV cache eviction pressure eased.

Eve (oncall): dashboards update: p99 down from 12.1s -> 3.4s (still above threshold). p95 back to 1.1s. keep monitoring for next 10m.

Mike (infra): temp fix complete. next action: cordon noisy node(s) and schedule tenant-998 to dedicated hosts tomorrow. I'll open infra ticket to pin them to dedicated-reserved for burst windows.

Sara (ML): long-term: recommend model quantization + KV cache tuning for tenant-998 and a suggested model profile in Optimize: reduce context window or enable persistent KV cache in Redis-backed store to avoid local NVMe thrash.

Eve (oncall): any signs this could be attacker or misconfiguration?

Mike (infra): logs show normal request patterns but high concurrency + large context. not malicious.

Josh (support): acme-inc replied with "thanks for quick fix, still seeing occasional blips but much better".

Eve (oncall): closing temporary mitigation in 20m once stable. Mike, please prepare rollback steps for cgroup and routing changes. Sara, can you add the failing prompt set to our quality regression monitor?

Sara (ML): will add prompt set and a synthetic test that reproduces tail stalls. Also capturing sample reqs for postmortem.

Mike (infra): rollback steps posted in infra ticket INF-3421. cgroup removal commands & routing rollback snippet:
```bash
# remove tenant cgroup
sudo cgdelete -g blkio:/noisy-tenant-998
# routing rollback (deploy-bot command)
redwood-cli routing set /v1/streaming/generate --tier enterprise --pool pooled-default
```

Eve (oncall): last check 10m after mitigation: p99=1.6s, p95=0.9s. marking incident as mitigated. preparing incident bridge for full RCA. assigning owners: infra=Mike, ML=Sara, support=Josh.

Anna (PM): schedule customer follow-up and include timeline + mitigations. I'll own comms.

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (temporary). Please file postmortem with timeline, root cause hypothesis (noisy tenant causing NVMe writeback thrash + KV cache eviction -> streaming stalls), and action items (permanent tenant isolation, model tuning suggestions, routing SLA changes).

Eve (oncall): thanks team. will run full postmortem template in incidents/postmortems. :white_check_mark:
